scenes.tts: If you sew one eye shut, what happens to the cortical cells it used to drive?
scenes.visual: Title card: Six Days at Four Weeks. A kitten's right eyelid closes. Convention: left hemisphere recorded; right eye (contralateral) orange, left eye (ipsilateral) blue; histograms run group 1 on the left to group 7 on the right.
scenes.narration: If you sew one eye shut, what happens to the cortical cells it used to drive?

scenes.tts: In nineteen sixty-three, Wiesel and Hubel reported what happens when a kitten grows up with one eye closed.
scenes.caption: In 1963, Wiesel and Hubel reported what happens when a kitten grows up with one eye closed.
scenes.visual: Credit: Wiesel and Hubel, 1963.
scenes.narration: In 1963, Wiesel and Hubel reported what happens when a kitten grows up with one eye closed.

scenes.tts: They sutured the lids of one eye at or near birth. They recorded after about three months of closure.
scenes.visual: A timeline: closure at or near birth, recording after about three months.
scenes.narration: They sutured the lids of one eye at or near birth. They recorded after about three months of closure.

scenes.tts: Very few cortical cells could be driven by the closed eye.
scenes.visual: The histogram empties on the closed eye's side. Schematic.
scenes.narration: Very few cortical cells could be driven by the closed eye.

scenes.tts: Yet its retina still responded. So did its L G N cells, though those serving the closed eye looked smaller.
scenes.caption: Yet its retina still responded. So did its LGN cells, though those serving the closed eye looked smaller.
scenes.visual: The closed eye's retina lights up to a flash. LGN cells for that eye respond but are drawn smaller.
scenes.narration: Yet its retina still responded. So did its LGN cells, though those serving the closed eye looked smaller.

scenes.tts: So the eye was not broken. What changed was in the brain.
scenes.visual: An arrow moves from the eye to the cortex. Label: the change is in the brain.
scenes.narration: So the eye was not broken. What changed was in the brain.

scenes.tts: An adult cat with one eye closed for months showed no such change.
scenes.visual: An adult cat with one eye closed for months; its histogram stays a normal hump.
scenes.narration: An adult cat with one eye closed for months showed no such change.

scenes.tts: In nineteen seventy they asked when. They closed one eye in kittens of different ages, for different lengths of time.
scenes.caption: In 1970 they asked when. They closed one eye in kittens of different ages, for different lengths of time.
scenes.visual: Credit: Hubel and Wiesel, 1970. A grid of kittens by age and length of closure.
scenes.narration: In 1970 they asked when. They closed one eye in kittens of different ages, for different lengths of time.

scenes.tts: Predict. That closure from birth lasted months, so it spanned many ages. Compare brief closures begun at different ages. Is there one switch-off point, or a rise and a fall?
scenes.visual: Question card: brief closures begun at different ages. One switch-off point, or a rise and a fall? Empty axes: effect of closure against age at closure.
scenes.narration: Predict. That closure from birth lasted months, so it spanned many ages. Compare brief closures begun at different ages. Is there one switch-off point, or a rise and a fall?

scenes.tts: A rise and a fall. In kittens, susceptibility began around the start of the fourth week.
scenes.visual: A curve rises from the start of week 4. Label: kitten.
scenes.narration: A rise and a fall. In kittens, susceptibility began around the start of the fourth week.

scenes.tts: It stayed high until somewhere between six and eight weeks. Then it declined through the third month.
scenes.visual: The curve holds high to between weeks 6 and 8, then falls through month 3. Label: kitten, schematic curve.
scenes.narration: It stayed high until somewhere between six and eight weeks. Then it declined through the third month.

scenes.tts: So a closure from birth lasting three months overlaps those weeks, which fits its large effect.
scenes.caption: So a closure from birth lasting 3 months overlaps those weeks, which fits its large effect.
scenes.visual: A bar for the 1963 closure, birth to month 3, laid over the curve; it covers the high weeks.
scenes.narration: So a closure from birth lasting 3 months overlaps those weeks, which fits its large effect.

scenes.tts: At the peak, the effect was fast. Some kittens had the right eye closed for only six days, in the fourth or fifth week.
scenes.caption: At the peak, the effect was fast. Some kittens had the right eye closed for only 6 days, in the fourth or fifth week.
scenes.visual: The right eye closes for 6 days during week 4 or 5, marked on the curve's peak.
scenes.narration: At the peak, the effect was fast. Some kittens had the right eye closed for only 6 days, in the fourth or fifth week.

scenes.tts: Recording in the left hemisphere, the closed right eye is the group one side.
scenes.caption: Recording in the left hemisphere, the closed right eye is the group 1 side.
scenes.visual: Electrode in the left hemisphere. The orange right eye is marked as the group 1 end of the scale.
scenes.narration: Recording in the left hemisphere, the closed right eye is the group 1 side.

scenes.tts: The number of cells it could drive fell to a fraction of normal. Most of the histogram moved toward group seven, the open eye.
scenes.caption: The number of cells it could drive fell to a fraction of normal. Most of the histogram moved toward group 7, the open eye.
scenes.visual: The bars slide toward group 7, the blue open-eye end. Schematic.
scenes.narration: The number of cells it could drive fell to a fraction of normal. Most of the histogram moved toward group 7, the open eye.

scenes.tts: Six days of unequal vision had been enough.
scenes.visual: Caption on screen: 6 days of unequal vision.
scenes.narration: Six days of unequal vision had been enough.

scenes.tts: The anatomy follows. Hubel, Wiesel and Simon LeVay closed one eye in infant macaque monkeys.
scenes.visual: Credit: Hubel, Wiesel and LeVay. An infant macaque with one eye closed.
scenes.narration: The anatomy follows. Hubel, Wiesel and Simon LeVay closed one eye in infant macaque monkeys.

scenes.tts: Later they traced the stripes in layer four C. The open eye's stripes had widened, and the closed eye's had narrowed.
scenes.caption: Later they traced the stripes in layer 4C. The open eye's stripes had widened, and the closed eye's had narrowed.
scenes.visual: Layer 4C stripes: the open eye's stripes widen, the closed eye's narrow.
scenes.narration: Later they traced the stripes in layer 4C. The open eye's stripes had widened, and the closed eye's had narrowed.

scenes.tts: In kittens, single thalamic axons serving a deprived eye were later seen to lose branches within about a week.
scenes.visual: One thalamic axon arbor for the closed eye loses branches over about a week.
scenes.narration: In kittens, single thalamic axons serving a deprived eye were later seen to lose branches within about a week.

scenes.tts: So a closure in this window changes the territory each eye's axons hold, not only how cells respond.
scenes.visual: Side by side: territory map and response histogram, both tilted toward the open eye.
scenes.narration: So a closure in this window changes the territory each eye's axons hold, not only how cells respond.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: in the young, a few days of unequal vision move the balance. In the adult, months do not.
scenes.visual: Closing card: young, days are enough; adult, months are not.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: in the young, a few days of unequal vision move the balance. In the adult, months do not.

scenes.tts: That leaves a question. Did the closed eye lose because it was unused, or because the other eye was not?
scenes.visual: Two labels appear: unused? or out-competed?
scenes.narration: That leaves a question. Did the closed eye lose because it was unused, or because the other eye was not?
